insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's beta network has confirmed $2.17M in GMV across 37,576+ receipts — each one a cryptographically verified purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. For CMOs paying $5+ CPM to reach audiences who might buy, this represents a fundamentally different data class: deterministic proof of transaction, not behavioral inference.

insights.topic: 14-day throughput as a live demand signal
insights.insight: $261,205 across 5,435 receipts in the trailing 14-day window puts average basket size at $48.05 — a computable, real-time measure of consumer spending by category and metro that updates at sub-hourly intervals. No survey, panel, or modeled dataset produces this resolution.

insights.topic: Category mix reveals where verified buyers actually spend
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets leads with 1,426 receipts at a $47.87 average basket; restaurants-dining follows at 1,297 receipts and $37.77 average. Together they represent 50.2% of 14-day receipt volume — a share that has been rising consistently, confirming that everyday consumable categories dominate verified purchase behavior in this network.

insights.topic: Average basket compression signals category shift, not demand softness
insights.insight: Average basket has compressed from ~$65 to ~$48 over the monitoring window — but the driver is category mix rotating toward grocery and dining, not unit price erosion or weakening demand. CMOs using basket size as a proxy for consumer health should weight category composition before drawing conclusions.

insights.topic: Brand-level receipt attribution is computable in real time
insights.insight: Walmart leads at 370 receipts in the 14-day window, followed by Costco at 166 and Target at 132 — brand-level purchase frequency visible without cookies, panels, or modeled attribution. This is the direct competitive intelligence layer that receipt-verified commerce enables for retail and CPG brand teams.

insights.topic: Evening accumulation pattern is structurally consistent
insights.insight: The 16:15–20:15 UTC window consistently produces the sharpest receipt accumulation — the 2026-06-28 peak of 5,472 receipts and $272,638 was set at 20:15, and the 2026-06-29T16:16 interval added 75 receipts in a single heartbeat. For brands running time-sensitive commerce campaigns, this cadence identifies when verified purchase activity is highest.
